questions.q: What does the transfer step actually do?
options: It deletes transactions from Receivables permanently
It moves summarized subledger journal entries into the General Ledger's own journal tables
It creates a new customer statement
It approves a write-off above a user's limit
questions.explain: Transfer moves the finalized, summarized journal entries from the Receivables subledger into GL's journal tables.

questions.q: How does posting differ from transferring?
options: They are the same action with two different names
Posting is the separate GL-side step that makes a journal entry final and updates account balances
Posting happens in Receivables before transfer, not after
Posting only applies to miscellaneous receipts
questions.explain: Posting is distinct from transferring — it is the action within GL that finalizes a journal entry and updates account balances.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of continuous transfer over period-end transfer?
options: It eliminates the need for Create Accounting
It provides near-real-time visibility into AR's impact on financials throughout the month
It is required by all Oracle Fusion implementations
It automatically resolves all reconciliation differences
questions.explain: Continuous transfer moves and posts entries throughout the month, giving near-real-time visibility rather than waiting for a single period-end batch.

questions.q: Which of these is a common reason the GL's Accounts Receivable balance might not match Receivables' own records?
options: A transaction failed to account and was never corrected
A customer statement was generated that month
A dunning letter was sent to a customer
An aging report was run using the 7-bucket method
questions.explain: An unaccounted transaction — one that failed Create Accounting and was never resolved — is a common source of a mismatch between GL and Receivables balances.

questions.q: Who typically decides whether a company uses continuous or period-end transfer?
options: Each individual AR clerk, transaction by transaction
The customer, based on their payment terms
This is decided during implementation as part of the company's close process design
It is fixed by Oracle and cannot be configured
questions.explain: The choice between continuous and period-end transfer is a close-process design decision made during implementation, not a per-transaction choice.
